papers.title: Shipyard pass
lines: Harland and Wolff, Queen's Island. Clock number 4417. In by half seven, out by five, tea at ten.
Written below: 'Da said you could hear the whistle in every street. Now you hear it in your head instead.'

papers.title: Letter home from school, 1981
lines: Dear parents, the bus to the swimming baths will go a longer way round on Thursday. There is no cause for worry.
Children are to bring their trunks, a towel and a sandwich. The teachers will bring the good humour.
Children from both schools will share the pool. Mrs Henderson says it is the only place anyone is allowed to shout.

papers.title: Letter from America, 1912
lines: Dear Mam, I am writing from a place called Boston, which is not unlike Cork except nobody knows me.
I have a job, a bed and a coat. I have everything except you. Send the rosary. I will send the money.
Tell Daddy I did not forget the garden.

trail.clue: A promise of twenty dollars sent home was never claimed. It is said to rest near the hedge.

papers.title: Factory note
lines: The Jacob's girls are on strike again, so the biscuits are late.
The Lord Mayor has promised a delegation, a cup of tea and a stern talking-to. The girls have promised nothing.

papers.title: Visitor's note
lines: The giant Finn built it to reach Scotland. The rival giant came the other way. A tale for tourists and for children.
Geologists say lava. The giant says rubbish. The giant has the better stories.

trail.clue: A guide's lucky horseshoe is buried near the big rock. 'I leave it for you, whoever you are.'

papers.title: Hurling programme
lines: The ball flies faster than the eye. The lads play hard and shake hands after.
Whoever wins, the match is not over until the tea is.

papers.title: Snug rules
lines: In the snug: the priest, the doctor, and anyone else who wishes to say something unwise.
No politics. No fighting. No remarks about the football. No exceptions, save on Sunday afternoons.

papers.title: Distiller's log
lines: Water from St Columb's Rill. Barley dried in a kiln, not in a peat fire. This is why ours is smooth and others are ... smokier.
The cat who keeps the warehouse mouse-free has been paid in cream for eleven years.

papers.title: Maiden voyage ticket
lines: Third class, Southampton to New York. A little cheaper than the rest, a little less glamorous, a lot more hopeful.
Written on the back in an unsteady hand: 'It is said she cannot sink. We shall see.' It is signed with a small drawing of a fish.

papers.title: Relief works note
lines: The relief works paid hungry men a few pennies to build roads that led nowhere. Some are still there, going straight on into the middle of a field.
Walk one slowly. Someone put their back into it, and they were not paid enough.
